description: Split mode Desk into two explicit sub-modes, per direct user steering: (a) the current 'copie / insertion' behaviour where Lya answers in the chat and the teacher inserts the result by hand, no file ever mutated; (b) 'mise à jour directe' where Lya updates the working file herself through the FEAT-002 file tools, and the Desk panel displays the working file at the top so the teacher always sees which file is about to be modified. Depends on FEAT-002 (it gates the tool loop that FEAT-002 adds).
steps: Backend plumbing (backend/internal/bridge/hermes.go): add a sub-mode field to the WS prompt message struct in HandleWebSocket, next to the existing Mode field. Name it DeskMode with json tag `deskMode`, accepted values "insert" and "direct". Thread it through startJob into callHermesStream (extend both signatures; startJob is only called from HandleWebSocket).

Backend gating: the FEAT-002 tool loop declares `tools` and executes read_file/write_file/patch_file ONLY when mode == "desk" AND the effective desk sub-mode is "direct". The v1.9.0 handleToolFileWrite interception must obey the same condition, so the copy/insert sub-mode can never mutate a file even if the model emits a write-flavoured hermes.tool.progress event.

Backward compatibility: an absent or unrecognised deskMode value must resolve to "direct", i.e. exactly the v1.9.x behaviour, so old frontends and the existing TestHermesBridge_FileWrite (which sends no deskMode) keep working. Document this default in a comment stating why it is not "insert": a silent switch to insert would make a deployed frontend stop writing files with no error.

Backend observability: include the effective sub-mode in the existing agent_usage log line (add deskMode=%s) and in the 'hermes: tool_calls supported=' diagnostic from FEAT-002, so production logs distinguish 'no tool calls because Hermes ignores tools' from 'no tool calls because the teacher was in insert mode'.

Backend tests (backend/internal/bridge/hermes_test.go): add (a) deskMode "insert" with a fake Hermes that returns a write_file tool call -> assert the request body carried NO tools key, no file was written, no file_changed event, and the job still reaches done; (b) deskMode "insert" with mockHermesFileWriteServer -> assert the tool progress event is still forwarded but no file is written (mirror of TestHermesBridge_FileWrite_LyaMode); (c) deskMode "direct" -> tools declared and the write happens; (d) deskMode absent -> same as direct (backward-compat guard).

Frontend state (frontend/src/components/Chat.tsx): add a Desk sub-mode selector rendered only when the component is in Desk mode (agent !== 'pi'), two options labelled from i18n, default 'insert' (the current, non-destructive behaviour). Send it in the prompt payload as deskMode alongside the existing mode field (see the sendPrompt payload around line 599 where mode is set to agent === 'pi' ? 'pi' : 'desk'). Persist the choice the same way the component already persists its session state if that is straightforward; otherwise keep it in local component state and say so in a comment.

Frontend working-file header: when the sub-mode is 'direct', render the current working file at the top of the Desk panel (use the existing currentFile prop, and an explicit i18n string when currentFile is null telling the teacher to open a file first). Style it with the existing CSS conventions in frontend/src/styles.css (vanilla CSS, custom properties, no CSS framework) and reuse existing chat header classes rather than inventing a new visual language.

While in the i18n files, fix the wording FEAT-003 flagged: the 'file updated' note rendered after a write reuses piChat.updated ('Fichier mis à jour par Pi.'), which names Pi even when Lya wrote the file in the direct sub-mode. Add a Lya-appropriate string and use it when the writer was the Desk/Lya agent, keeping the pi wording for the pi agent.

Frontend i18n: add the sub-mode labels, a short explanation of each, and the working-file header strings to BOTH frontend/src/i18n/fr.json and frontend/src/i18n/en.json under the existing chat/desk section, keeping the key naming style of the surrounding entries. FR is the default UI language.

Do NOT change frontend/src/components/LyaChat.tsx (mode Lya stays pure conversation, no sub-mode, no file access) and do NOT change backend/internal/bridge/pi.go. Do NOT remove buildDeskPrompt or MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS: the inlining stays active in BOTH sub-modes, since it is the working fallback for reading the open file.

Frontend tests (frontend/src/components/Chat.test.tsx, existing style): assert (a) the default sub-mode is copie/insertion and the prompt payload carries deskMode:'insert'; (b) after selecting the direct sub-mode the payload carries deskMode:'direct'; (c) in the direct sub-mode the working file path is displayed at the top of the panel; (d) in the direct sub-mode with currentFile null the 'open a file first' string is displayed; (e) the sub-mode selector is not rendered in Lya mode (add to LyaChat.test.tsx if that is where the assertion belongs).

Verify by mutation: (1) force the backend gate to ignore the sub-mode and confirm the insert-mode backend tests fail; (2) flip the frontend default to 'direct' and confirm the default-sub-mode test fails; (3) drop the working-file header and confirm its test fails. Restore after each and record in findings which test caught which mutation.

Run the full verification (backend go build/vet/gofmt/test, frontend vitest + npm run build) and commit with a conventional message such as 'feat: deux sous-modes en mode Desk (copie/insertion et mise à jour directe)'. Do not push, do not touch version.json.
acceptance_criteria: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./... -count=1 -timeout=90s passes with no gofmt output
cd frontend && npx vitest --run passes and npm run build succeeds
With deskMode 'insert', the Hermes request body contains no tools key, no file on disk is created or modified, no file_changed event is emitted, and the job still completes normally
With deskMode 'direct', the tools are declared and read_file/write_file/patch_file execute as in FEAT-002
An absent deskMode behaves exactly like 'direct', and TestHermesBridge_FileWrite (which sends no deskMode) still passes unchanged
The Desk panel shows the working file path at the top when the direct sub-mode is selected, and an explicit message when no file is open
The default sub-mode on first render is copie/insertion, and the prompt payload reflects the selected sub-mode
New UI strings exist in both fr.json and en.json with no missing-key fallbacks rendered in the tests
LyaChat.tsx and backend/internal/bridge/pi.go are unchanged (git diff shows nothing for either), and buildDeskPrompt plus MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS are intact
verification: cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./... -count=1 -timeout=90s
cd frontend && npx vitest --run && npm run build

findings:
Commit 8d37559. Backend: msg.DeskMode (json deskMode) -> startJob -> callHermesStream -> streamTurn; normalizeDeskMode() maps insert (case/space-insensitive) to insert and everything else (absent, unknown) to direct, with the comment explaining why the default is not insert. fileToolsEnabled(mode, deskMode) is still the single gate and now also gates the v1.9.0 handleToolFileWrite interception in streamTurn (was `mode == "desk"`). deskMode added to the agent_usage line, to the 'hermes: tool_calls supported=' line and to the 'refusing unsolicited tool call(s)' line. Frontend: ChatSession gained optional deskSubMode (persisted for free because App/MobileLayout hold ChatSession opaquely, so the choice survives the tab/mode-switch unmounts; separate deskSession and piSession already exist), exported type DeskSubMode and DEFAULT_DESK_SUB_MODE = 'insert'; payload always carries deskMode; segmented selector (.chat-submode*, same look as .toolbar-mode-switcher) and the working-file banner (.chat-workfile, .chat-workfile--none) render only when agent !== 'pi', banner only in direct. New i18n keys under chat.: subModeLabel, subModeInsert, subModeDirect, subModeInsertHint, subModeDirectHint, workingFile, noWorkingFile, updated (fr + en). FEAT-003's flagged wording fixed: the write note now uses chat.updated ('Fichier mis à jour par Lya.') for the Desk/Lya agent and keeps piChat.updated for pi; the existing FEAT-003 test assertion was updated accordingly. Test helper: runHermesJob now delegates to runHermesJobSub(t, b, prompt, mode, deskMode) and still sends NO deskMode field, so every pre-existing desk test doubles as the backward-compat guard; TestHermesBridge_FileWrite untouched and still green. New backend tests: ToolLoop_InsertSubModeDeclaresNoTools, FileWrite_InsertSubMode, ToolLoop_DirectSubModeWrites, ToolLoop_AbsentSubModeIsDirect, TestNormalizeDeskMode. New frontend tests: 5 in Chat.test.tsx + 1 in LyaChat.test.tsx. Verification: backend go build/vet/gofmt (no output)/test all ok (3 packages); frontend 8 files / 90 tests (was 84) and npm run build ok. Mutation testing (backup kept inside the repo and restored in the same command, /tmp does not persist): (1) fileToolsEnabled reverted to `mode == "desk" && b.workDir != ""` -> TestHermesBridge_ToolLoop_InsertSubModeDeclaresNoTools failed on all 5 assertions (tools declared, tool_choice sent, 2 requests, file written, file_changed emitted) and TestHermesBridge_FileWrite_InsertSubMode failed on file_changed + file written, proving both gates are covered; (2) DEFAULT_DESK_SUB_MODE flipped to 'direct' -> 'defaults to the copie/insertion sub-mode and sends deskMode insert' failed, plus 'shows the working file at the top of the panel in the direct sub-mode' failed on its 'not shown in insert' pre-assertion; (3) working-file header replaced by {false && (...)} -> 'shows the working file at the top...' and 'tells the teacher to open a file when the direct sub-mode has none' both failed. pi.go, LyaChat.tsx and version.json are untouched (git diff empty), buildDeskPrompt and MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS intact (6 occurrences in Chat.tsx). Not pushed, not tagged, no release.

REVIEW PASS v1 (2025-08-24-200500-review.md) — sub-mode dispositions, mutation-verified:
- Issue 1 (BLOCKING: the Desk prompt contradicted the declared tools): FIXED. buildDeskPrompt now takes the sub-mode and only the context LINE changes: in `insert` the v1.9.1 wording is kept verbatim ("tu n'as pas accès à mon dossier de travail, ne cherche pas à l'ouvrir"), in `direct` it states that the file can also be re-read and edited with read_file/write_file/patch_file and asks for patch_file rather than text to copy. The inlining and MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS are untouched in BOTH sub-modes: the content is still the fallback for a gateway that drops `tools`, and it saves a read_file round-trip when it does not. Tests: Chat.test.tsx 'mode Desk keeps the "no file access" wording in copie/insertion' and 'mode Desk announces the file tools in the direct sub-mode, and still inlines the file' (which also re-asserts the inlined content and the trailing question).
- Issue 5 (v1.9.1 write path silently off by default): PARTIALLY FIXED, and the rest is deliberately out of this agent's scope. Two things changed: (a) the backend now keeps the v1.9.0 write interception for any client that sends no deskMode (deskModeLegacy, see FEAT-002 issue 4), so upgrading the backend alone changes nothing for an old frontend; (b) the sub-mode hint is now RENDERED under the selector (.chat-submode-hint) instead of living only in a title attribute, which is unreachable on a touch screen, and the insert hint explicitly points at « Mise à jour directe ». The release note itself is not written here: this agent must not bump version.json, tag or release, so the note belongs to the release the orchestrator owns. Test: Chat.test.tsx 'shows what the selected sub-mode does, and where to find the direct one'.
- Issue 13 (editor buffer reload discards unsaved edits): FIXED. The predicate moved to frontend/src/editorSync.ts (shouldReloadBuffer) and App.handleFileChanged only reloads when the buffer is clean; the file tree still refreshes either way. Extracted rather than inlined because App.tsx has no test harness (no App.test.tsx, and rendering it drags in Milkdown and the WebSocket), so an inline guard would have been untestable. Documented trade-off: when the buffer is dirty the editor and the disk diverge and the next auto-save writes the teacher's version over Lya's — the teacher's unsaved text is the only content that exists nowhere else, and Lya's version can be asked for again. Deliberately no UI banner: App has no toast/notice infrastructure and adding one would have grown the change well past the review's ask (an i18n string drafted for it was removed rather than left dead in fr.json/en.json). Tests: editorSync.test.ts (4 cases: clean reload, dirty kept, other file, no file open).
